Is a Penalty Quadratic in the Coefficients?

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
beta_quadratic.Rd

Returns TRUE when \(\partial^3\rho/\partial\beta^3\) is exactly zero, so that a consumer can skip that third derivative. The value comes from a method of the class of the penalty, so a consumer does not have to test the property numerically.

Usage

beta_quadratic(penalty, theta, ...)

Arguments

penalty

A penalty() object.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same, holding every name in penalty@params. The generic checks it as penalty_dhessian() does, so a missing hyperparameter or a value outside its open bounds is an error on every branch. The separable branch evaluates the parent at it, and the other branches return a constant without reading its values.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

A single logical. The base class returns FALSE, so a penalty class without a method of its own is treated as needing the third derivative.

Three independent properties

This predicate differs from is_quadratic(), which reports whether the penalty is a quadratic form whose matrix, rank and log pseudo-determinant are available through penalty_matrix() and its siblings. The two predicates and the linearity of \(S\) in \(\theta\) are independent properties:

penaltyis_quadratic()beta_quadratic()\(S\) linear in \(\theta\)
quadratic_penalty()TRUETRUEyes
structured_penalty()TRUETRUEno
additive_penalty()TRUETRUEyes
a Gaussian distrib_penalty()FALSETRUEno
heavy_penalty()FALSEFALSEno

The method of the separable branch

The log-density is quadratic in the response exactly when its second derivative in the response does not depend on the response. The method therefore evaluates distributions7::distrib_hess_y() of the parent at four points and tests whether the values agree across the points with all.equal() at a tolerance of 1e-12, which is a relative tolerance. The method does not compute a third derivative. The page beta_quadratic.DistribPenalty() describes the points and the multivariate case.

The meaning of TRUE

TRUE does not imply that the marginal derivatives are available. A lasso gives TRUE, because its log-density is linear in the response away from the kink, and penalty_dhessian() still signals an error for it: the third derivative is zero where it exists and undefined at the kink, and a selecting fit places its coefficients at the kink.

See also

is_quadratic() for the property of the construction, penalty_dhessian_beta() for the derivative that is zero when this is TRUE, penalty_hessian() for the Hessian that is then constant in the coefficients.

Examples

# These are two of the three branches that give TRUE for both predicates.
beta_quadratic(quadratic_penalty(diag(3)), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] TRUE
beta_quadratic(structured_penalty(
  parameters7::log_cholesky(2)),
  list(log_L1 = 0, log_L2 = 0, L2.1 = 0))
#> [1] TRUE

# A Gaussian prior is quadratic in beta and is not a quadratic penalty.
g <- distrib_penalty(
  distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), mu = 0),
  n_coef = 3)
c(beta_quadratic(g, list(sigma = 1)), is_quadratic(g))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE

# A Student t prior is neither.
beta_quadratic(heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))
#> [1] FALSE

# And TRUE does not mean the marginal derivatives exist.
beta_quadratic(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] TRUE
try(penalty_dhessian(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), c(1, 0, -1),
                     list(lambda = 1)))
#> Error : 'separable [fixed laplace2 [mu=0]]' has a kink, so penalty_dhessian() does not exist there and
#>   its hyperparameters cannot be estimated by a marginal criterion.
